items.text: Know the preparation of aromatic amines by the reduction of aromatic nitro-compounds using tin and concentrated hydrochloric acid.

items.label: text
items.text: These nitrogen-containing compoundshave some similaritieswith ammonia. The three bonding pairs of electrons around nitrogen are distributed in a trigonalpyramidalshape.Thenitrogen atom has a lone pair of electrons and three bonds to one or more alkyl groups. If there is one alkyl group, the amine is classed as primary. If there aretwo,thenit issecondary.Withthree itistertiary.FigAshows thestructuresofthesimplestamineineachoftheseclasses.

items.label: text
items.text: In this book we will focus on primary amines. Methylamine is a gas at room temperature,ethylamine has a boiling temperature of 17 °C, and propylamine and butylamine are volatile liquids. This list of names shows the naming system used -the suffix is -amine and the usual codes methyl, ethyl, propyl, butyl etc. are used.

items.label: text
items.text: We will also meet the simplest aromatic amine, CHsNH2, which is phenylamine.

items.label: text
items.text: Amines occur widely in nature,and many drugs (bothlegal and illegal) are amines, including the group of compounds called amphetamines.

items.label: text
items.text: We learned about amines in Topic 10 (Book 1: IAS),but only as the product of reactions between halogenoalkanes and ammonia.
